choices.text: In an interface VPC endpoint for the SageMaker Runtime API created in the database's VPC for the model to use
In a new field of the endpoint configuration's production variant that lists the subnets used by the variant's instances
In the `VpcConfig` of the SageMaker model (CreateModel), which the endpoint's containers use for their network interfaces
In the VPC settings of the SageMaker Studio domain that the engineer used to write and deploy the IaC template

stem: A central tooling account (A) stores a private inference image in Amazon ECR. SageMaker endpoints in a workload account (B) must pull that image, and the image must not be made public. Which TWO configurations are required? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A repository policy on the ECR repository in account A that allows account B's SageMaker execution role to pull the image
An S3 bucket policy in account A that grants account B read access to the bucket where ECR stores the image layers
A resource share in AWS RAM that shares the ECR repository from account A with account B through AWS Organizations
A VPC peering connection between the two accounts' VPCs so SageMaker in account B can reach the ECR registry in account A
An IAM policy on the SageMaker execution role in account B that allows the ECR pull actions on the repository in account A

stem: A CodePipeline in a shared DevOps account deploys a SageMaker endpoint stack with a CloudFormation action into a separate production account. The deploy action fails because the production account cannot read the pipeline's artifacts in S3. Which TWO changes are required? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Keep the default AWS managed `aws/s3` key and add the production account to the artifact bucket's ACL as a grantee
Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication from the artifact bucket to a bucket in the production account before each deploy
Encrypt the artifact bucket with a customer managed KMS key whose key policy allows the production account to use it
Move the whole pipeline into the production account so the artifacts never have to cross an account boundary
Create an IAM role in the production account that trusts the DevOps account and set it as the deploy action's role

stem: The same SageMaker Pipeline definition must run in dev with `ml.m5.large` instances and 10% sample data, and in prod with `ml.p3.2xlarge` instances and full data, without maintaining two copies of the pipeline code. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Keep two Git branches with different hard-coded instance types and data paths and deploy whichever branch matches the account
Store the values in a notebook that edits the pipeline's JSON definition by hand before each run in the target account
Create two separate pipelines with different names and copy every step definition from the dev pipeline into the prod pipeline
Define `ParameterString` values for the instance type and input path and override them in `pipeline.start()` for each environment

stem: Data scientists have tested Python functions for preprocessing, training and evaluation in notebooks. They want to turn them into a SageMaker Pipeline with minimal rewriting, keeping the functions as plain Python. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Schedule the notebooks with cron on a SageMaker notebook instance so they run one after the other in the required order
Decorate the functions with the `@step` decorator from the SageMaker Python SDK and build the pipeline from the step outputs
Rewrite every function as a separate Docker image and reference each image from its own custom container processing step
Convert the functions into AWS Lambda functions and chain them with Lambda steps, since Lambda runs plain Python code

stem: A large model runs on a real-time endpoint with 16 GPU instances. The team wants guarded updates with automatic rollback on CloudWatch alarms, but the account's GPU quota cannot fit a second full fleet during the update. Which deployment option fits BEST?

choices.text: A rolling deployment that replaces instances in small batches, with alarms that trigger an automatic rollback if they fire
Deleting the endpoint and creating a new one with the updated model, followed by a manual check of the CloudWatch alarms
A blue/green update with all-at-once traffic shifting, because it provisions the new fleet and switches traffic in a single step
A blue/green update with canary traffic shifting that sends 10% of traffic to a full new fleet before the remaining 90% moves

stem: A company wants an internal assistant on Amazon Bedrock that answers employee questions from 40,000 policy documents. About 200 documents change every day, answers must cite the source document, and the team has no labeled question-answer pairs. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Create an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base over the documents and answer with retrieval-augmented generation that returns citations
Fine-tune a Bedrock foundation model every night on the full document set so that the model memorizes the newest policy wording
Run continued pre-training every week on the changed documents so the model absorbs the new policy text before users ask about it
Paste as many complete policy documents as fit into every prompt so the model can read the relevant text directly for each question

stem: An online bank wants to flag logins where a customer account signs in from an IP address that is unusual for that particular account. It has 18 months of login logs with account IDs and IPv4 addresses but no labeled fraud examples. Which SageMaker built-in algorithm fits BEST?

choices.text: Random Cut Forest, trained on the IPv4 addresses converted to integers to find outlying address values
XGBoost, trained as a binary classifier on the login logs to predict which sign-ins are fraudulent ones
IP Insights, trained on account ID and IP address pairs to score how unusual each new pairing is
K-means, trained on the IPv4 octets to group addresses and flag logins that fall into the small clusters

stem: A manufacturer wants to extract its own part numbers (such as `HX-4471-B`) and internal failure codes from 300,000 free-text technician notes. Amazon Comprehend's standard entity detection does not return these as distinct types. The team has lists of known part numbers and codes but no ML engineers. Which option fits BEST?

choices.text: Amazon Comprehend topic modeling run on the notes so that part numbers and failure codes are grouped together into their own topics
Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognition trained with the existing entity lists for the part numbers and the failure codes
Amazon Textract with Queries that ask for the part number and failure code in each note that has been stored as a plain text file
The Comprehend DetectEntities API with the COMMERCIAL_ITEM entity type selected so that every part number is labeled correctly

stem: A SageMaker hyperparameter tuning job runs a custom PyTorch script. Every training job completes, but the tuning job shows no objective metric values. The metric definition uses the regex `val_loss=([0-9\.]+)`, and the script's log lines look like `epoch 5 validation loss: 0.2310`. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Enable SageMaker Debugger on the training jobs so that it collects the validation loss tensors and passes them to the tuner
Increase MaxRuntimeInSeconds for each training job so the script has enough time to write its final validation metric line
Change the tuning strategy from Bayesian to random search so that the objective metric does not need to be read from the logs
Fix the metric definition regex, or the script's log format, so the regex matches the validation loss lines the script prints

stem: An image model trained on one GPU with batch size 64 and learning rate 0.01 reaches 91% accuracy. The team moves to SageMaker distributed data parallel on 8 GPUs, keeping 64 images per GPU, the same learning rate and the same 30 epochs. Training is 7 times faster, but accuracy drops to 84%. The team wants to keep the speedup. What should it change FIRST?

choices.text: Scale the learning rate up in proportion to the larger global batch, with a short warm-up period at the start of training
Switch from data parallelism to model parallelism so that each GPU holds a part of the model instead of a full copy
Increase the number of epochs from 30 to 240 so that the model receives as many weight updates as it did on one GPU
Lower the per-GPU batch size to 8 so that the global batch size across all eight GPUs goes back to the original 64

stem: A single-instance SageMaker training job reads 1.5 TB of images from S3 in File mode. Each run spends about 40 minutes copying data before the first epoch starts. The training script opens image files from a local directory, and the team does not want to change how it reads data or build new storage infrastructure. Which change fits BEST?

choices.text: Increase the job's VolumeSizeInGB so that the full dataset copy completes faster on a larger ML storage volume before training
Switch the input channel to Pipe mode so that data is streamed from S3 directly into the training container as it is needed
Switch the input channel to FastFile mode so that S3 objects appear as local files and are streamed on demand while training
Set the channel's S3DataDistributionType to ShardedByS3Key so that the instance downloads only a portion of the objects in S3

stem: A fraud model uses the SageMaker built-in XGBoost algorithm with `objective=binary:logistic`. Only 0.8% of training rows are fraud. With `eval_metric=error` and early stopping, the model predicts almost no fraud, yet validation error is only 0.8%. Which TWO changes are MOST appropriate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Remove early stopping and set `num_round` to 5,000 so that the trees keep learning until they finally fit the fraud rows
Set `eval_metric` to `aucpr` so that early stopping and model selection track how well fraud cases are ranked
Change the objective to `multi:softmax` with `num_class=2` so that the two classes are learned as separate outputs
Set `subsample` to 0.1 so that each boosting round sees fewer legitimate rows and the classes appear more balanced
Set `scale_pos_weight` to about the ratio of negative to positive rows so that errors on fraud rows weigh more

stem: A tuning job for a gradient boosting model searches 8 continuous hyperparameters with the Bayesian strategy, `MaxNumberOfTrainingJobs=100` and `MaxParallelTrainingJobs=100`. The best result is no better than what random search found earlier. Which change is MOST likely to improve the Bayesian search?

choices.text: Enable warm start from the earlier random search and also raise MaxParallelTrainingJobs to 200 to explore more combinations
Set the scaling type of every hyperparameter to Logarithmic so that the search explores a wider range of values in each run
Switch to the grid search strategy so that every combination of the eight continuous hyperparameters is tried at least once
Lower MaxParallelTrainingJobs to a small number, such as 5, so each new batch of jobs can use the results of completed jobs

stem: A team must adapt a 13-billion-parameter open language model to its support-ticket style on SageMaker. Its budget allows one ml.g5.2xlarge instance with a single 24 GB GPU. Full fine-tuning runs out of GPU memory immediately. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Full fine-tuning with batch size 1 and gradient checkpointing so that activations are recomputed and the whole model fits in memory
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning with LoRA adapters on a 4-bit quantized copy of the base model (QLoRA) so only small adapters train
Full fine-tuning with a much larger dropout rate so that fewer neurons are active in each step and the memory needed is much lower
Pre-training a new 13-billion-parameter model from scratch on the support tickets so that the whole model learns the company style

stem: Before training a loan-approval model, a compliance team wants to know whether the historical labels already approve applicants aged 60 or over at a lower rate than younger applicants. No model exists yet. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Run a SageMaker Clarify post-training bias analysis and review Disparate Impact (DI) for predictions made on the age facet
Run a SageMaker Clarify pre-training bias analysis and review the Class Imbalance (CI) metric for the age facet in the data
Run a SageMaker Clarify pre-training bias analysis and review the Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL) for the age facet
Schedule SageMaker Model Monitor bias drift monitoring on the endpoint and alarm when the age-group metrics begin to differ

stem: Instance metrics show that a PyTorch image training job on an ml.p3.8xlarge instance keeps GPU utilization around 25%. One CPU core is at 100% while the others are mostly idle, and the DataLoader decodes and resizes full-size JPEGs every epoch. Which TWO actions will MOST improve GPU utilization? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Resize and encode the images once in a SageMaker Processing job so the training job reads smaller, ready-to-use inputs every epoch
Split the model across the GPUs with model parallelism so that each GPU runs fewer layers and waits less for every training batch
Move the training job to an ml.p4d.24xlarge instance so that the model has faster GPUs with more memory available for each batch
Increase the learning rate and the number of epochs so that the GPUs perform more useful work each time a new batch reaches them
Increase the DataLoader `num_workers` so that several CPU processes decode and augment images in parallel with the training steps

stem: A team has fine-tuned two candidate models for summarizing support conversations and wants to compare them on 2,000 prompts for correctness, completeness and helpfulness. ROUGE scores do not reflect quality well, and no human reviewers are available. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: An Amazon Bedrock programmatic evaluation job that scores the similarity of each summary to a set of reference summaries
An Amazon Bedrock model evaluation job that uses a human-based workflow with a work team made up of the company's own employees
Amazon CloudWatch metrics for each model's invocation latency and output token count, compared over several days of test traffic
An Amazon Bedrock model evaluation job that uses a judge model (LLM-as-a-judge) to score each response on the chosen metrics

stem: A credit model's SageMaker Clarify SHAP report is confusing: nearly every applicant gets a large positive attribution for `age` and `income`. The analysis configuration uses a baseline record where every feature, including age and income, is set to 0. What should the engineer change?

choices.text: Use a representative baseline, such as a summary of the training data from K-means centroids, instead of the all-zero record
Remove `age` and `income` from the model inputs so that the other features receive a fairer share of every applicant attribution
Replace SHAP with partial dependence plots so that each feature's average effect is shown without having to use any baseline
Increase `num_samples` in the SHAP configuration so the Kernel SHAP estimates become more precise for every applicant record

stem: A model scores 5 million insurance records every night with a SageMaker batch transform job, and no real-time endpoint exists. The team wants automated reports and alerts when the input feature distributions drift from the training baseline. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Create CloudWatch anomaly detection alarms on the batch transform job's duration and instance CPU utilization for every nightly run
Deploy a real-time endpoint only to enable data capture, send each night's records through it, and attach a Model Monitor schedule
Enable data capture in the batch transform job and create a Model Monitor data quality schedule that reads the captured batch data
Run a SageMaker Clarify explainability job every night on the scored output and compare the global SHAP values with the last run

stem: A day after a new mobile app release, the `Invocation4XXErrors` metric of a SageMaker real-time endpoint jumps, while `Invocation5XXErrors`, `ModelLatency` and CPU utilization stay unchanged. The model and endpoint were not modified. What should the team do FIRST?

choices.text: Raise the container's model server timeout and worker count so that long-running requests from the new app have more time to finish
Increase the endpoint's instance count and lower the auto scaling target value so that more capacity absorbs the new mobile traffic
Roll the endpoint back to the previous model version because the new release has exposed a defect inside the model artifact itself
Compare the new app's request payloads and ContentType with what the container expects, using the endpoint logs for rejected calls

stem: A Model Monitor data quality schedule runs hourly on an endpoint with 60 features. The team wants a CloudWatch alarm only when the drift distance of two critical features, `credit_utilization` and `income`, exceeds a threshold, not for every violation in the report. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Create an EventBridge rule on the monitoring job's completion event and send every completed execution to an SNS topic for review
Enable CloudWatch metrics publishing in the monitoring schedule and alarm on the drift metrics for those two features only
Configure a CloudWatch Logs metric filter that counts every violation line in the monitoring job logs and alarm when it exceeds 1
Enable an alarm on the endpoint's Invocations metric so the team is notified whenever the request volume changes significantly

stem: Several internal applications call foundation models through the Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel and Converse APIs. Compliance now requires keeping the full prompt and response text of every call for one year, searchable for investigations. Which solution fits BEST?

choices.text: Create CloudWatch dashboards for the Bedrock Invocations, InputTokenCount and OutputTokenCount metrics with one year of retention
Enable Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging with delivery to Amazon S3 and CloudWatch Logs, and set the retention periods to one year
Create an AWS CloudTrail trail for all Regions that stores Bedrock API events in S3, and query the stored events with Amazon Athena
Attach an Amazon Bedrock guardrail to every application's calls so that each prompt and response is filtered and stored before return

stem: An endpoint captures 100% of requests and responses, about 2 TB per day in S3, for hourly data quality and daily model quality monitoring. Captured data is never used after 30 days, and storage cost is rising fast. Which TWO changes reduce cost while keeping both kinds of monitoring? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add an S3 Lifecycle rule that expires captured objects older than 30 days under the endpoint's data capture prefix in the bucket
Change the data capture options to capture only the request input so that the stored response data is no longer kept in the bucket
Suspend the monitoring schedules on weekends so that the monitoring jobs do not read captured data on Saturdays and Sundays
Add an S3 Lifecycle rule that moves captured objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive as soon as they are written to the capture prefix
Lower the data capture sampling percentage to a level, such as 10%, that still gives each monitoring run a representative sample

stem: A SaaS company has 900 small XGBoost models, one per tenant, each on its own ml.m5.large real-time endpoint that is under 3% utilized. All models use the same container. The company wants to cut hosting cost and the number of endpoints to manage, and an occasional slower first request for a rarely used tenant is acceptable. Which option fits BEST?

choices.text: Keep one endpoint per tenant but switch every endpoint to an ml.t2.medium instance so that each tenant's endpoint costs much less
Combine the 900 models into one multi-container endpoint so that each tenant model runs in its own container behind one endpoint
Host all tenant models on a small number of SageMaker multi-model endpoints that load each model from S3 when a request needs it
Move every tenant model to its own serverless inference endpoint so that each tenant is billed only for the requests that it sends

stem: Data scientists use SageMaker Studio JupyterLab spaces on ml.g5.xlarge instances. Cost reports show many of these apps running all night and through weekends with no activity. Administrators want an automatic control that does not depend on users remembering to stop apps. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Send a daily email reminder with Amazon SNS each evening that asks every user to stop the running JupyterLab applications
Buy a SageMaker Savings Plan that covers the ml.g5.xlarge usage so that the hours spent idle are billed at a lower rate
Reduce the default EBS volume size of each JupyterLab space so that the storage attached to the idle apps costs much less
Configure idle shutdown for JupyterLab apps in the SageMaker domain settings with an idle timeout such as 60 minutes

stem: Each data science team has its own sandbox AWS account in AWS Organizations. When a sandbox account's actual monthly spend passes its budget, finance wants new SageMaker training jobs and endpoints in that account blocked automatically until an administrator reviews it. Which solution fits BEST?

choices.text: Cost Explorer forecasts reviewed every week by the finance team, who then manually delete SageMaker resources in any overspending account
An AWS Budgets budget per account with a budget action that applies an SCP denying SageMaker create actions when the budget is exceeded
Service Quotas requests that lower each sandbox account's SageMaker instance quotas so that the accounts cannot run many instances
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection monitors for each sandbox account that send alerts to the finance team whenever unusual spend patterns appear

stem: A training data bucket has a policy that denies all S3 access unless `aws:SourceVpce` equals the VPC's S3 gateway endpoint. Studio notebooks in the VPC read the data fine, but SageMaker training jobs now fail with AccessDenied even though their execution role allows `s3:GetObject`. The jobs are created without a VpcConfig. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Add `s3:ListBucket` and `s3:GetObject` for the bucket to the execution role again so that the role permissions are refreshed
Change the bucket's default encryption to SSE-KMS and grant the execution role kms:Decrypt so the training data can be read
Run the training jobs with a VpcConfig that uses subnets whose route tables include the S3 gateway endpoint for the data bucket
Enable network isolation on the training jobs so that SageMaker downloads the training data only over the private AWS network

stem: A bank's SageMaker Studio domain must meet two rules: users may open Studio only from the corporate network range 198.51.100.0/24, and traffic from Studio apps must not use SageMaker-managed internet access. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add an `aws:SourceIp` condition for 198.51.100.0/24 to the IAM policy that allows `sagemaker:CreatePresignedDomainUrl` for users
Attach an AWS WAF web ACL to the Studio domain with an IP set rule so that only requests from 198.51.100.0/24 can reach the domain
Add an inbound security group rule on the Studio subnets that allows HTTPS only from 198.51.100.0/24 for all user browser sessions
Lower SessionExpirationDurationInSeconds for the presigned domain URLs so that each user's Studio session must be renewed more often
Set the domain's network access type to VpcOnly so that all Studio app traffic flows through the bank's own VPC, subnets and endpoints

stem: A security team must guarantee that every SageMaker training job in an account encrypts its attached ML storage volumes with a customer managed KMS key and runs inside a VPC. Jobs that do not comply must be rejected at creation. Which TWO IAM policy conditions should deny `sagemaker:CreateTrainingJob`? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Deny when the `aws:SecureTransport` condition key is false, so that the job and all of its data stay inside of the company VPC
Deny when the `sagemaker:InterContainerTrafficEncryption` key is false, so that the job's data is encrypted on its storage volumes
Deny when the `sagemaker:NetworkIsolation` condition key is false, so that the training job must be launched inside a VPC
Deny when the `sagemaker:VpcSubnets` condition key is null, so that jobs created without subnets from a VPC are rejected
Deny when the `sagemaker:VolumeKmsKey` condition key is null, so that jobs without a KMS key for their storage volumes are rejected

stem: A SageMaker Processing job needs a database password to read features from an Amazon RDS instance. The password is currently passed in the job's environment variables, and a security review found it in plain text in DescribeProcessingJob output. Which change fixes this BEST?

choices.text: Store the password in a String parameter of Systems Manager Parameter Store and pass only the parameter name to the processing job
Build the password into the processing container image and store that image in a private Amazon ECR repository with scanning on
Pass the password as a container argument instead of an environment variable so that it no longer appears in the job settings
Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager, pass only the secret name, and let the job's execution role read the secret at runtime
